claim: In an Eisenberg–Noe star clearing network with \(m\ge1\) targets, unit outside assets, equal initial net worth \(x\in(0,1/(m+1))\) for every bank, and a source whose liabilities are entirely interbank and split equally among the targets, let independent primary loss shocks share survival function \(S\) and be capped at the unit outside-asset value. If \(S(0)=1\) and \(\log S\) is convex on \([0,(m+1)x]\), then the probability that a shock to the source alone defaults all targets is \(S((m+1)x)\ge S(x)^{m+1}\), the probability that all banks default through independent direct shocks. The inequality is strict when \(\log S\) is strictly convex on the relevant interval; in particular, every non-degenerate mixture of exponential rates gives strict inequality at every feasible threshold, while a pure exponential law gives equality.

integrity.numerical_witness: Two-rate mixture with rates 1 and 10, equal weights, \(m=1,\ x=1/5\).
integrity.proof_basis: Analytic convexity proof; numeric script is illustrative only.

scientific_limitations: Acyclic star network only; source financial connectivity is one and its liabilities are equally allocated.
All banks have unit outside assets and equal positive initial net worth \(x\), with \((m+1)x<1\).
Independent primary shocks share a common log-convex survival function and realized losses are capped at unit outside assets.
The result compares the probability of all targets defaulting from one source shock with simultaneous independent direct defaults; it does not compare aggregate loss magnitudes or correlated shocks.
title: A sharp distributional boundary for default contagion under log-convex shock survival
